 New-Look FC Goa Test Unbeaten NorthEast United In Guwahati
 New-Look FC Goa Test Unbeaten NorthEast United In Guwahati 
 20 Nov, 2026 Share Share Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on WhatsApp Copy Link Close Highlanders Put Five-Match Unbeaten Run On The Line As Spanish Tactician Ángel Viadero Takes Charge Of Gaurs For The First Time. 
 Guwahati: NorthEast United FC will look to extend their unbeaten start to the MG Indian Super League 2026-27 when they host FC Goa at the Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium on Saturday, 21 November. The Highlanders have collected 11 points from five matches and conceded just twice, making them the league's most defensively solid side so far. 
 Juan Pedro Benali's men have recorded wins over Mohun Bagan Super Giant, Kerala Blasters FC and Churchill Brothers FC Goa, alongside draws against Odisha FC and Bengaluru FC. Their defensive organisation has been central to this run, with goalkeeper Gurmeet Singh recording 19 saves and three clean sheets. At the other end, Alaaeddine Ajaraie, Jithin MS and Antonio Moyano have scored twice each. 
 Saturday's fixture, however, brings a different challenge, with FC Goa arriving under new head coach Ángel Viadero. The Spaniard, who previously worked alongside Benali at NorthEast United, takes charge of the Gaurs for the first time, adding a personal dimension to the contest. The two coaches share a 25-year friendship, having worked together at four different clubs. 
 Viadero is well aware of the challenge awaiting his side, describing NorthEast United as “possibly the team that has the clearest way to play and win”. He also praised Benali, calling the Highlanders “a very well-armed team, with an extraordinary coach”. Despite having had only three training sessions with his new squad, Viadero is determined to make an immediate impact. “I want the team to compete from the get-go. I want it to be a serious team from the upcoming match itself. I want us to look for a win immediately,” he said. 
 Benali, meanwhile, expects his former colleague to bring changes to Goa's approach but believes his side can adapt. Reflecting on their friendship, he said, “Angel is one of my best friends. We’ve been friends for 25 years now. We've worked together in four different teams.” On the tactical uncertainty, he added, “I know he will try to surprise us. But the surprise will be in the first 10 minutes. After that, we can adjust our gameplay.” 
 FC Goa are seventh with five points from four matches. They have drawn against Chennaiyin FC and Sporting Club Delhi, beaten Inter Kashi 2-1 and lost 2-1 to Bengaluru FC. Francisco ‘Franchu’ Feuillassier has scored twice and provided an assist, while Christian ‘Chiki’ Borrego has also found the net twice. 
 NorthEast United will have to manage some fitness concerns, with Benali confirming that Asheer Akhtar is hospitalised with dengue, while Nikola Ninković and Samte Buanthanglun are injured. 
 With the Highlanders looking to preserve their unbeaten run and Viadero beginning a new chapter with Goa, Saturday's meeting promises an exciting reunion. Kick-off is at 7:30 PM IST, with live coverage on the MG ISL YouTube channel and Sony Sports Network.
